Content.task: Use plain language and avoid figures of speech, idioms, and complicated metaphors
Make sure that `button`, `a`, and `label` element content is unique and descriptive
Use left-aligned text for left-to-right (LTR) languages, and right-aligned text for right-to-left (RTL) languages

Global code.task: Use a `lang` attribute on the `html` element
Provide a unique `title` for each page or view
Ensure that viewport zoom is not disabled
Use landmark elements to indicate important content regions

Keyboard.task: Make sure there is a visible focus style for interactive elements that are navigated to via keyboard input
Check to see that keyboard focus order matches the visual layout

Images.task: Make sure that all `img` elements have an `alt` attribute
Make sure that decorative images use null `alt` (empty) attribute values
Provide a text alternative for complex images such as charts, graphs, and maps
For images containing text, make sure the alt description includes the image’s text

Headings.task: Use heading elements to introduce content
Use only one `h1` element per page or view
Heading elements should be written in a logical sequence

Lists.task: Use list elements (`ol`, `ul`, `dl`) for list content

Controls.task: Ensure that links are recognizable as links
Provide a skip link and make sure that it is visible when focused
Identify links that open in a new tab or window

Tables.task: Use the `table` element to describe tabular data
Use the `th` element for table headers (with appropriate `scope` attributes)
Use the `caption` element to provide a title for the table

Forms.task: All inputs in a form are associated with a corresponding `label` element
Make sure that form input errors are displayed in list above the form after submission
Associate input error messaging with the input it corresponds to
Make sure that error, warning, and success states are not visually communicated by just color

Media.task: Make sure that media does not autoplay
Ensure that media controls use appropriate markup
Check to see that all media can be paused

Appearance.task: Check your content in specialized browsing modes
Double-check that good proximity between content is maintained
Make sure color isn’t the only way information is conveyed
Make sure instructions are not visual or audio-only
Use a simple, straightforward, and consistent layout

Animation.task: Ensure animations are subtle and do not flash too much
Provide a mechanism to pause background video
Make sure all animation obeys the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query

Color contrast.task: Check the contrast for all normal-sized text
Check the contrast for all large-sized text
Check the contrast for all icons
Check the contrast of borders for input elements (text input, radio, checkboxes, etc.)
Check text that overlaps images or video

Mobile and touch.task: Check that the site can be rotated to any orientation
Ensure that button and link icons can be activated with ease
Ensure sufficient space between interactive items in order to provide a scroll area

levels.A: Essential — If this isn’t met, assistive technology may not be able to read, understand, or fully operate the page or view
levels.AA: Ideal Support — Required for multiple government and public body websites
levels.AAA: Specialized Support — typically reserved for parts of websites for a specialized audience

notes.disclaimer: This checklist covers many, but not all, level A and AA concerns. It does not guarantee a site is fully accessible.
